about: Examples of what a tracker could pick up for this family, to show one possible structure: what happened, which moment it is (market, rule, life or decision), what it touches in this family's plan, and where in the case data to look. Nothing is invented: a past market shock already in the family's data, the official 2027 tax changes, and a dated moment from the family's plan. They are not today's news and not a list of what to build: what to watch, and from which sources, is up to you. Amounts are US dollars.

signals.source: Past market event in this family's investment analysis
signals.headline: Liberation Day tariffs announced: the S&P 500 lost 10% in two days
signals.what_happened: The US announced broad reciprocal tariffs (a 10% baseline, 34% on China, 20% on the EU). The S&P 500 lost 10% in two days. Full description in analysis.events.
touches_this_family: This portfolio fell 7.1%, against 6.2% for a simple mix with the same stock share. On today's $360,000 of investments and cash, a fall that size is about $25,600.
Worst fall in the last three years: 9.2%, recovered in 37 days.
Longer history: in the Global Financial Crisis (Oct 2007 to Mar 2009) the current mix would have lost 16.8% and the recommended mix 6.1%; in the COVID crash (Feb to Mar 2020) 11.2% and 7.7%.
Technology is 30.0% of Timothy and Melanie's stock holdings, mostly through VTI.
Timothy's Roth IRA holds $12,740 of UPRO, a leveraged fund that aims for three times the daily move of the S&P 500 (persona D4b).
$150,000 of the total is cash, which does not fall with the market.

signals.headline: 2027 tax values published: standard deduction, brackets, child tax credit, Social Security wage base
signals.what_happened: The IRS published the 2027 inflation adjustments on 5 November 2026: standard deduction $16,600 single and $33,200 married filing jointly (from $16,100 and $32,200), brackets indexed, child tax credit $2,300 per child (from $2,200). The Social Security wage base rises to $192,300 for 2027 (from $184,500). They apply from 1 January 2027.
touches_this_family: Married filing jointly: standard deduction rises by $1,000, from $32,200 to $33,200.
Child tax credit rises by $100 per child for Liam (6) and Josh (3): $200 a year more; their $270,000 of salaries is below the $400,000 phase-out start.
Both salaries ($150,000 and $120,000) are below the wage base, so the Social Security change does not raise their payroll tax.
where_in_the_data: legal-values.json (same file as legal/legal-dataset-sample.json): StandardDeductionByYear, FederalIncomeTaxBracketsByYear, ChildTaxCreditByYear, SSWageBaseByYear
sources: SSA contribution and benefit base 2027: $192,300 (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html; 2027 COLA fact sheet https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html)

signals.headline: The plan's first move: pay down the 18% card from cash
signals.what_happened: The card carries $18,000 at 18% with $300 a month paid, about $270 of it interest; at that pace it is paid off in September 2039. The plan's first move pays it down from cash.
touches_this_family: Accessible cash is $150,800, about 16 months of essential expenses against a recommended 8 to 9 months; cash above the reserve and the yearly vacation is $60,222.50 (persona D3).
Timothy is Growth and Melanie is Moderate; a plan should be explained so both can follow it (case.household, persona D5).
